prospects.name: Renée J. James
prospects.uo_connection: BA International Business 1986; MBA 1992, both from University of Oregon. Current UO Board of Trustees member.
prospects.current_role: Founder and former Chairman/CEO of Ampere Computing; Operating Executive at The Carlyle Group; independent director at Citigroup; former President of Intel
prospects.wealth_sources: 28-year career at Intel (rose to President); founder/CEO of Ampere Computing, a semiconductor (Arm server chip) company sold to SoftBank for $6.5B in 2025; private equity (Carlyle); board compensation (Citigroup, formerly Oracle/Vodafone)
prospects.recent_news: On March 19, 2025, SoftBank Group announced acquisition of Ampere Computing for $6.5 billion in an all-cash deal, set to close in the second half of 2025. As Ampere's founder and major equity holder, James experienced a significant liquidity event.
prospects.athletics_connection: No publicly documented athletics gift to date; serves on UO Board of Trustees, giving her direct institutional engagement with university leadership and priorities.
prospects.philanthropy_history: Active institutional leadership via UO Board of Trustees; longtime tech-industry civic/government service (NSTAC chair under Obama). Specific large philanthropic gifts not widely publicized, suggesting untapped major-gift potential.
prospects.why_prospect: James just monetized a multi-billion-dollar company she founded, creating a fresh, large liquidity event ideal for a transformational gift. As a current UO Trustee with two UO degrees, she has deep institutional loyalty and is already engaged with university leadership. Her capacity and recent windfall make her one of the strongest new athletics prospects.
prospects.engagement_angle: Leverage her Board of Trustees relationships and President Scholz's office. Frame an athletics gift around innovation, women's sports leadership, or a technology/performance-science angle (e.g., student-athlete performance analytics) that aligns with her semiconductor/AI background and Ducks pride.
prospects.urgency_flag: HIGH — the $6.5B SoftBank acquisition closed in 2025, creating a near-term liquidity window. Engage promptly while proceeds and tax-planning conversations are active.

prospects.recent_news: Chuck Lillis died September 10, 2024; the Lillis family legacy and foundation remain active. The passing creates an estate/legacy-giving moment for Gwen and the family foundation.

prospects.engagement_angle: Approach through the UO Foundation and President's office with a tribute concept honoring Chuck Lillis's legacy as inaugural Board chair — potentially a named athletics facility space or leadership/scholarship fund bridging academics and athletics.

prospects.recent_news: Continues as a founding principal of Division Street, the Phil Knight-backed UO NIL collective (active 2021-present), placing him at the center of UO's NIL/revenue-sharing strategy. Continues leading K2 and Seaview insurance ventures.
prospects.athletics_connection: Exceptionally deep: former UO AD; reinstated baseball and led PK Park development; drove the Matthew Knight Arena project; donated $3M for locker-room renovation, $5M toward PK Park, $1M for the Matthew Knight Arena floor, $1.5M for arena design; estimated $15-20M total to UO.

prospects.urgency_flag: College athletics' shift to revenue-sharing/NIL (a Division Street focus) is an active window where his leadership and capital are most relevant right now.

prospects.estimated_net_worth: $500M-$1B+ (Roseburg Forest Products is one of the largest family-held wood-products corporations in the U.S.)
prospects.wealth_sources: Roseburg Forest Products — large privately held forest-products/timber company founded by Allyn's father Ken Ford in 1936; banking (Umpqua Bank chairmanship); Ramberg family glass business.
prospects.recent_news: In December 2024, the Fords made a $16M gift to OHSU Doernbecher Children's Hospital — the largest personal donation they have made to date and the single largest private gift in Doernbecher's 98-year history.
prospects.athletics_connection: The Fords' philanthropy explicitly includes support of UO Intercollegiate Athletics (cited by UO alongside the alumni center, art museum and Pacific Hall). Cheryl's deep alumni-leadership ties give Athletics a natural relationship pathway.
prospects.philanthropy_history: Lead donors of the Ford Alumni Center; $7M to renovate UO's Pacific Hall (2016); $16M to OHSU Doernbecher (2024); $5M+ endowed deanship and $6M faculty endowment at OSU; 750+ scholarships funded via the Ford Family Foundation.
prospects.why_prospect: A profoundly UO-loyal family (Cheryl is past Alumni Association president and Foundation trustee) with very substantial private wealth and a fresh, escalating major-gift cadence (the $16M Doernbecher gift shows current eight-figure capacity and willingness).
prospects.engagement_angle: Engage Cheryl through her alumni-leadership legacy and the family's pattern of naming/endowment gifts; the recent Doernbecher gift was driven by personal/family meaning, so tie an athletics opportunity to family legacy and Oregon community impact.
prospects.urgency_flag: The Dec 2024 $16M gift demonstrates they are actively making their largest-ever gifts now — a prime cultivation window.

prospects.name: Jordan Schnitzer
prospects.uo_connection: Earned an undergraduate degree at the University of Oregon (then Lewis & Clark Law School); namesake/donor of the Jordan Schnitzer Museum of Art at UO; serves on the boards tied to UO arts (museum)
prospects.current_role: President & CEO, Schnitzer Properties (formerly Harsch Investment Properties); President, Harold & Arlene Schnitzer CARE Foundation; President, Jordan Schnitzer Family Foundation
prospects.giving_capacity: $5M-$10M+ to UO (athletics would be a new direction)
prospects.wealth_sources: Commercial real estate — grew the family firm (founded 1950) to 31M+ sq ft across six Western states; one of the top 10 private real estate owners in the West. Also a world-renowned fine-art print collector.
prospects.recent_news: Schnitzer Properties continues aggressive industrial expansion (seven projects totaling 2.25M sq ft across OR/AZ/CA/NV; ~$59M Seattle-area purchases). Company celebrated its 75th anniversary in 2025. He is the main donor of the new Schnitzer School of Art at Portland State.
prospects.athletics_connection: No known UO Athletics giving — his UO philanthropy is concentrated in the arts (Jordan Schnitzer Museum of Art). He represents a major-capacity UO alumnus whose giving could potentially be broadened, though athletics is not his demonstrated interest.
prospects.philanthropy_history: Namesake/donor of three Jordan Schnitzer Museums of Art (UO, PSU, WSU); main donor of PSU's Schnitzer School of Art; Schnitzer Cares youth grantmaking ($5.2M+ to 563 Oregon nonprofits); 2012 Simon Benson Award for philanthropy.
prospects.why_prospect: A billion-dollar UO alumnus with a deep, named philanthropic relationship to the university and a clear pattern of large, legacy-naming gifts. While his demonstrated passion is the arts, his capacity and UO loyalty make him worth strategic cultivation for any university priority.
prospects.engagement_angle: Lead with university-wide partnership and legacy naming (his established preference) rather than a pure athletics pitch; explore a cross-cutting opportunity (e.g., athletics + arts/culture, student-athlete spaces, or campus placemaking) that fits his identity as a builder and collector.
prospects.urgency_flag: Company's 75th anniversary (2025) and active expansion suggest strong liquidity and a legacy-minded moment.
